Let $T=[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ What is the image of the square $R$ (shown above) above under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Looking at the matrix $T$, we can see that $T$ represents a horizontal shear of shear factor $\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore, the image of the square $R$ under $T$ is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/85ff90a404a22310659fadd3a00c58490c9745d443b180d6b509b40a5497376b.png)

**Alternative method:**

We can check that the vertices of $R$ are mapped to the vertices of the parallelogram shown above as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
